terms.comment: A description of ours: crusta is any hard coat laid over a surface (see “crust”), and the icing is made of saccharum pulvereum (see “icing sugar”). We have found no word for icing in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. The Roman glaze was honey: Cato brushes his cakes with it when they come out (melle unguitō, Cato Agr. 76), and Petronius’s tart has hot honey poured over it. To spread icing on, indūcere, to draw a coat over a surface (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: We’ll spread icing over the cake.

phrases.latin: Ubi cocta erit, eximitō et melle unguitō.
phrases.english: When it is baked, take it out and brush it with honey.

sources: Lewis & Short: crusta · Lewis & Short: saccharon · Lewis & Short: induco
